title: Mary P NDE 5269
content: I came into the emergency room with bad chest pains. After being initially evaluated, one of the Emergency Medical Technicians was trying to put in an IV into my vein (my veins are hard to get). The part I remember was telling him that I felt a bit sheepish, as the pain was almost gone. He assured me I was doing the right thing. The part I don't remember, and what the hospital staff told me later, is that I arched my back, saying, 'Oh God, it's happening again!' I was hooked up to an electrocardiogram and the alarm went off then. As this was going on, I found myself sitting at an almost picnic-looking table and bench. We were near some trees I'd never seen, which I found out much later were olive trees. Sitting to my side were people that I felt I was supposed to know, but couldn't make out their features. The colors I saw were beyond description, as if color had tone, touch, and meaning. Across from me sat a man, who I could see much more clearly than everything else did. He looked Mediterranean - black hair, and the most gentle dark brown eyes I had ever seen (on Earth at least). When he began communicating with me, it wasn't verbal. I could hear him in my mind. He explained he came to me dressed as a modern, clean-cut human because he knew me, and (he made a bit of a joke) that if he had come in the 'Robes' (his words) that I wouldn't have believed it and would have thought I had gone crazy. It seems we started having a laughing argument over something, and I realize I was asking to stay. He was laughing and smiling, and he pointed his finger at me. The next I knew the world looked horribly dull, and there was a person's face close up to mine, asking if I knew my name. At that point, I still wasn't sure of anything. Then she asked if I knew where I was. I looked beyond her and saw many people wearing medical gear, and I said, 'No.' When she told me the name of the hospital, however, it clicked. I said, 'Yes, I came because my chest hurt', and they all looked relieved. The doctor that took over said I had only been 'gone' about 30 seconds. I didn't tell her, but I was thinking, 'How could that have been? It seemed longer!' I feel that this happened to prepare me for my daughter trying to kill herself nearly a year later, after her dad tried to re-marry. They say she took too much Tylenol for her liver, and they gave up on her. Her stepfather and I prayed over her all night. My faith in Christ had been renewed by his gentle smile and him 'winning' (as he said) whether I stayed or went. My daughter made, as they put in her records, a miraculous recovery. She is still alive and still healthy.
